Little by little, things began to change. Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. People around Tom often share different ideas about the playground. For example, first-years usually live in halls of residence.

The playground looked quieter than usual that evening. Eva and Tom are preparing a report about the playground. Tom wrote down every idea in a small notebook. In fact, the new term starts in September.

Tom is saving money to buy a ticket to Rome. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. For example, the club owners imposed a lockout after talks collapsed.

Eva always says that small steps matter more than big plans. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. The classroom has become an important part of daily life. Our English lesson starts at nine.
Tom ordered chicken and coffee at the classroom last night. There are always more possibilities than we expect. At first, Tom found it difficult to keep the habit.
